Judgment calls: (a) ADDED COMPONENT id 23, GND at ~(221,353). A ground symbol is unmistakably drawn there in exactly the same style as GNDs 12/14/16/17/22 (vertical bar with tick plates to its left, wire leaving to the right) and it is absent from the bootstrap inventory. Its wire runs right to x=250 then down into Op-Amp 8's left (non-inverting) input. Even without the appended component the net is 0. (b) The vertical at x~436 that carries n7 is a faint pencil line that binarisation broke into three pieces: y=35..89 (down from V-DC 3), the corner/branch at y=107, and y=108..129. There is an 18 px gap at y=89..107 and a 13 px gap at y=129..142 (the Op-Amp 1 top edge). I read it as ONE continuous lead, because (i) the fragments are collinear to within 3 px in x, (ii) Op-Amp 1 has no other visible inverting-input lead, and (iii) any other reading strands V-DC 3 with a dangling terminal and leaves Op-Amp 1's second input unconnected. So V-DC 3 +, Capacitor 7 top and Op-Amp 1 in- are one net. (c) Op-Amp polarity: none of the five triangles carries an explicit +/- pin marking - the glyph inside each is the gain label '+1'. All five are drawn apex-down with two leads on the top edge. I read the LEFT top lead as in+ (index 0), the RIGHT top lead as in- (index 1) and the apex as out (index 2). This is the electrically sensible reading and is uniform across the sheet: for Op-Amps 0, 1, 4 and 8 the left lead goes straight to a GND symbol while the right lead is the one carrying the feedback element (R21 for 4, C7 for 1, R18 for 0, C15 for 8); for Op-Amp 2 the left lead takes the signal from n2 and the right lead carries the R6/L11 feedback. (d) The crossing-free reading of the x~270 column was checked at 20x: both marks at (270,181) and (270,190) are clean T-junctions onto the same vertical (no hop, no gap), so Op-Amp 4's output, Resistor 21's bottom, Capacitor 13's top and Resistor 20's top are all one node. (e) The filled blob on the bottom rail at (250,497) is a pen dwell where the drafter re-inked the rail (the trace visibly thickens to its right); nothing else terminates there, so it is not a junction. (f) 2-terminal parts are listed in drawn order (top-then-bottom for the vertical ones, left-then-right for V-DC 3 and I-DC 10, whose left terminals face their GND symbols); this does not affect any metric. (g) Tier-2 note: n11 has no DC path to ground except through the op-amp outputs, and n7 sits between a voltage source and a capacitor. Both are exactly what the ink shows and are left as drawn.
